'''''Equals Pi''''' is a painting created by American artist [[Jean-Michel Basquiat]] in 1982. The painting was published in ''[[GQ]]'' magazine in 1983 and ''[[W (magazine)|W]]'' magazine in 2018.<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal|last1=Carlsen|first1=Peter|last2=Smith|first2=Philip|date=March 1983|title=The Next Wave Art: Electrically Electric|journal=GQ|pages=227}}</ref><ref name=":5" />

==History==
''Equals Pi'' was executed by Jean-Michel Basquiat in 1982, which is considered his most coveted year.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Gotthardt|first=Alexxa|date=2018-04-01|title=What Makes 1982 Basquiat's Most Valuable Year|url=https://www.artsy.net/article/artsy-editorial-1982-basquiats-valuable-year|access-date=2021-08-23|website=Artsy|language=en|archive-date=2020-05-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200525160138/https://www.artsy.net/article/artsy-editorial-1982-basquiats-valuable-year|url-status=live}}</ref> The [[robin egg blue]] painting contains Basquiat's signature crown motif and a head alongside his characteristic scrawled text with phrases such as "AMORITE," "TEN YEN" and "DUNCE."<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|last=Villa|first=Angelica|date=2021-08-23|title=Beyoncé and Jay-Z Pose with Long-Unseen Basquiat in Tiffany Campaign|url=https://www.artnews.com/art-news/market/beyonce-jay-z-tiffany-basquiat-1234602125/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-08-24|website=ARTnews.com|language=en-US|archive-date=2021-08-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210824030548/https://www.artnews.com/art-news/market/beyonce-jay-z-tiffany-basquiat-1234602125/}}</ref> The title refers to the mathematical equations incorporated on the right side of the work. The cone refers to the pointed [[Dunce|dunce caps]] depicted in the work.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Sayej|first=Nadja|date=August 23, 2021|title=Beyoncé And Jay-Z Pose Alongside Rare Basquiat Painting In Jewelry Ad|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/nadjasayej/2021/08/23/beyonc-and-jay-z-pose-alongside-rare-basquiat-painting-in-jewelry-ad/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-09-02|website=Forbes|language=en|archive-date=2021-09-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210902013826/https://www.forbes.com/sites/nadjasayej/2021/08/23/beyonc-and-jay-z-pose-alongside-rare-basquiat-painting-in-jewelry-ad/}}</ref>

The painting was acquired in 1982 by Anne Dayton, the advertising manager of ''[[Artforum]]'' magazine.<ref name=":6">{{Cite news|last=Friedman|first=Vanessa|date=2021-09-01|title=The Mystery of That Basquiat Painting — and Its Tiffany Blue|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/09/01/style/tiffany-basquiat-jay-z-beyonce.html|access-date=2021-11-09|issn=0362-4331|archive-date=2021-11-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211109001040/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/09/01/style/tiffany-basquiat-jay-z-beyonce.html|url-status=live}}</ref> She purchased it for $7,000 from Basquiat's exhibition at the [[Fun Gallery]] in the [[East Village, Manhattan|East Village]].<ref name=":6" /> At the time the painting was called ''Still Pi''. However, when the work appeared in the March 1983 issue of ''[[GQ]]'' magazine, it was titled ''Knowledge of the Cone'', which is written on the top of the painting.<ref name=":4" /> 

According to reports in August 2021, the luxury jewelry brand [[Tiffany & Co.]] had recently acquired the painting privately from the Sabbadini family, for a price in the range of $15 million to $20 million.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Kinsella|first=Eileen|date=August 23, 2021|title=Here's the Little-Known History of the Robin's Egg Blue Basquiat Painting That Stars in Beyoncé and Jay-Z's New Tiffany Ad|url=https://news.artnet.com/art-world/tiffany-unveils-new-ad-campaign-starring-beyonce-and-basquiat-2001708|url-status=live|access-date=2021-08-24|website=Artnet News|language=en-US|archive-date=2021-08-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210823211422/https://news.artnet.com/art-world/tiffany-unveils-new-ad-campaign-starring-beyonce-and-basquiat-2001708}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Socha|first=Miles|date=August 23, 2021|title=EXCLUSIVE: Beyoncé and Jay-Z Meet a Blue Basquiat in Tiffany's New Campaign|url=https://wwd.com/accessories-news/jewelry/beyonce-jay-z-tiffany-ad-campaign-1234900967/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-08-24|website=WWD|language=en-US|archive-date=2021-08-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210824002113/https://wwd.com/accessories-news/jewelry/beyonce-jay-z-tiffany-ad-campaign-1234900967/}}</ref> The painting, which is largely in the brand's signature blue color, is displayed in the [[Tiffany & Co. flagship store|Tiffany & Co. Landmark store]] on [[Fifth Avenue]] in New York City.<ref name=nyt-2023-04-20>{{Cite news|last=Vadukul|first=Alex|date=2023-04-20|title=The New Tiffany, Unboxed|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/04/20/style/tiffany-fifth-avenue-store.html|access-date=2023-04-28|issn=0362-4331|archive-date=2023-04-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230427084836/https://www.nytimes.com/2023/04/20/style/tiffany-fifth-avenue-store.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Although initial reports claimed that the painting had never been seen before, it had previously been offered at auction twice and had appeared in magazines.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=Holmes|first=Helen|date=2021-08-23|title=A Never-Before-Seen Basquiat Is the Star of Beyoncé and Jay-Z's New Tiffany's Ad|url=https://observer.com/2021/08/basquiat-beyonce-jay-z-tiffanys/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-08-23|website=Observer|language=en-US|archive-date=2021-08-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210824020759/https://observer.com/2021/08/basquiat-beyonce-jay-z-tiffanys/}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> The work was first offered at a [[Sotheby's]] sale in [[London]] in June 1990, where it went unsold.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Liscia|first=Valentina Di|date=August 24, 2021|title=Tiffany's Wants You to Think It Inspired a Blue Basquiat Painting|url=http://hyperallergic.com/671927/tiffanys-wants-you-to-think-they-inspired-a-blue-basquiat-painting/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-08-25|website=Hyperallergic|language=en-US|archive-date=2021-08-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210824235306/https://hyperallergic.com/671927/tiffanys-wants-you-to-think-they-inspired-a-blue-basquiat-painting/}}</ref> In December 1996, the Sabbadinis, a [[Milan]]-based clan behind the eponymous jewelry house, purchased it at a Sotheby's London auction for $253,000.<ref>{{Cite magazine|last=Freeman|first=Nate|date=August 24, 2021|title=The Curious History of the Basquiat in That Jay-Z and Beyoncé Tiffany Ad|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/style/2021/08/basquiat-jay-z-beyonce-tiffany|access-date=2021-08-26|magazine=Vanity Fair|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":3" /> Mother and daughter Stefania and Micól Sabbadini posed in front of the painting in their living room for a 2018 feature in ''W'' magazine.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|last=Hoare|first=Philip|date=August 14, 2018|title=Go Inside the Understated Yet Eccentric Milan Home of the Fabulous Sabbadini Family|url=https://www.wmagazine.com/story/sabbadini-milan-home|url-status=live|access-date=2021-08-24|website=W ==Use in Tiffany & Co. campaign==
In 2021, luxury jewelry company [[Tiffany & Co.]] partnered with American singer [[Beyoncé]] and rapper [[Jay-Z]] to promote the company's "About Love" campaign. In the campaign, Jay-Z is seen wearing his hair much like Basquiat posing in front of ''Equals Pi''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Beyoncé and JAY-Z x Tiffany: About Love {{!}} Tiffany & Co. |url=https://www.tiffany.co.uk/stories/guide/beyonce-and-jay-z-about-love/ |access-date=2023-12-25 |website=www.tiffany.co.uk}}</ref> The campaign was used to showcase the company's new art purchase, as the painting features a color close to the company's signature [[Tiffany Blue]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Friedman |first=Vanessa |date=2021-09-01 |title=The Mystery of That Basquiat Painting — and Its Tiffany Blue |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/09/01/style/tiffany-basquiat-jay-z-beyonce.html |access-date=2023-12-25 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> 

The campaign was met with criticism from the artist's former friends and colleagues.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |last=Baker |first=Sinéad |title=Basquiat's friends and collaborators say they are 'horrified' by Beyoncé and Jay-Z's Tiffany campaign with his art |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/basquiat-friends-collaborators-horrified-beyonce-jay-z-tiffany-ad-2021-9 |access-date=2024-01-11 |website=Business Insider |language=en-US}}</ref> Stephen Torton, a former assistant of Basquiat's, posted a statement on [[Instagram]] saying, "I designed and built stretchers, painted backgrounds, glued drawings down on canvas, chauffeured, traveled extensively, spoke freely about many topics and worked endless hours side by side in silence. The idea that this blue background, which I mixed and applied was in any way related to [[Tiffany Blue]] is so absurd that at first I chose not to comment. But this very perverse appropriation of the artist's inspiration is too much."<ref name=":6" />

Furthermore, a curator of Basquiat's work has stated that if the use of this shade of blue was in reference to Tiffany, it would have been intended as criticism rather than an homage or as something to be commercialized by the company.<ref name=":7" />
